text:
olivia: Hey team — noticed on my 03/31 paystub that my contributions show 7% pre-tax and 3% Roth but my portal election is 10% Roth only. Looks like vendor split it wrong. I hit Roth limit last year and wanted Roth again this year. Can we fix before year-to-date totals get messed up?

noah (People Ops): Thanks for flagging, @olivia. That sounds like a mapping/translation issue between the portal election and payroll file. Can you DM a screenshot of the portal election page and the paystub? We'll start a vendor ticket.

olivia: DM'd both. Paystub shows employee deferral 10% pre-tax, Roth 0%. Portal clearly shows 100% Roth.

amy (Finance): Quick note on tax/totals: if deferrals were posted pre-tax instead of Roth, we can reclassify contributions at the plan/vender level (recharacterize Roth <-> pre-tax) for the affected pay periods, but it depends on vendor support and timing. If we reclassify after the reporting period closes, it may require W-2 correction. So the sooner we fix, the better.

ben (Benefits Vendor): Vendor here. We see the payroll file with contribution type code "PRE" for ID 48xx instead of "ROTH". That mapping came from the payroll vendor's feed. We can accept a reclassification request to adjust contribution type for 03/15 and 03/31 pay periods. For any changes, we need: 1) People Ops ticket with employee ID and pay periods, 2) signed reclassification consent from participant, and 3) payroll confirmation that amounts are available to move (i.e., no distribution occurred).

olivia: Signed consent? Is that just a checkbox in the portal or a signed PDF?

noah (People Ops): For audit trail we ask participants to sign the "Contribution Reclassification Authorization.pdf" and upload to the portal or email hr-benefits@redwood.com. We'll attach that to the vendor ticket.

benefits-portal-bot: Benefits Portal: Upload received: Contribution Reclassification Authorization.pdf for user olivia. Reference CP-2219. Vendor ACK pending.

payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: Off-cycle reclassifications or manual reversals must be requested by 04/07 18:00 PT to avoid W-2 adjustments for Q1 reporting. If request arrives later, we may need to issue corrected W-2 (W-2C) depending on tax-year impacts.

amy (Finance): After vendor reclassifies, Payroll will need to update tax reporting and YTD boxes. If we can get vendor ACK before the quarterly reporting close we'll avoid a W-2C. Also note: Roth<->pre-tax reclassifications can affect pre-tax limits and elective deferral caps; we'll validate you didn't exceed annual pre-tax limit after reclass. If you did, we may need to process an excess deferral distribution per IRS rules.

noah (People Ops): Action plan: 1) We received your signed authorization (thanks). 2) People Ops will open a formal vendor ticket with CP-2219 and attach paystubs. 3) Vendor to reclassify 03/15 and 03/31 contributions to Roth. 4) Payroll to confirm tax reporting consequences. We'll keep you posted in this thread.

ben (Benefits Vendor): Confirmed — starting reclassification process. ETA 2 business days. If payroll can confirm funds not distributed, we'll proceed.

amy (Finance): Confirming payroll has not distributed any amounts beyond normal withholdings; funds are still in plan trust and available for reclassification. We'll stand by to update reporting after vendor confirmation.

olivia: Huge relief — thank you. Two clarifying Qs: 1) Will this change my taxable wages for these paychecks? 2) Will my Roth deferral limit be affected if vendor reclassifies to Roth now?

amy (Finance): 1) Pre-tax vs Roth affects taxable wage reporting at payroll: if reclassified to Roth, those cents will be treated as taxable wages in the original pay periods. The reclassification will adjust payroll records so net pay isn't retroactively changed but W-2 boxes are updated as needed. 2) Roth limit is based on elective deferrals designated Roth. We'll recalculate your YTD elective deferral Roth amount after reclass. If you are approaching the Roth limit, we'll notify you and discuss corrective steps (excess distribution or other remediations).

noah (People Ops): Ben, please post vendor confirmation once done and include CP-2219. Olivia we'll DM a quick checklist for what to expect on the W-2 timeline.

ben (Benefits Vendor): CP-2219 done. Reclassification completed for pay periods 03/15 and 03/31. Updated participant record. Confirmation email sent to People Ops. Ref bv-2219.

noah (People Ops): Got the vendor confirmation. Forwarding to payroll for final steps.

payroll-bot: Payroll: Received reclassification request and vendor confirmation. We'll update payroll tax reporting and confirm whether a W-2 correction is required. Expect final status in 1-2 business days.

olivia: Thanks everyone  appreciate the speedy help. Please let me know if you need any more signed forms.
